title: Upper-tail ring colimits and compatible tensor base-change identifications
statement: Let $R,B$ be commutative rings with $B$ an $R$-algebra, $I$ a nonempty directed preorder, and $(S_i,a_{ij})$ a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras with colimit $(S,a_i)$ in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Work in a common universe containing the index and all ring carriers. Fix $i\in I$ and put $J_i=\{j\in I\mid i\le j\}$. Then $(S,(a_j)_{j\in J_i})$ is a colimit of the restricted diagram both in commutative $R$-algebras and in commutative rings: for every commutative ring $U$ and compatible ring maps $b_j:S_j\to U$ for $j\in J_i$, there is exactly one ring map $b:S\to U$ with $ba_j=b_j$. Set $D_j=S_j\otimes_R B$ and $D=S\otimes_R B$, with algebra multiplication $(s\otimes x)(s'\otimes x')=ss'\otimes xx'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $T=S_j$ with $j\ge i$, and for $T=S$, give $T$ its $S_i$-algebra structure through the transition or coprojection $\alpha_T:S_i\to T$. There are $T$-algebra isomorphisms $\theta_T:T\otimes_{S_i}D_i\xrightarrow{\sim}T\otimes_R B$ and $\lambda_T:T\otimes_{S_i}S_i\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ with $\theta_T(t\otimes(s\otimes x))=t\alpha_T(s)\otimes x$, $\theta_T^{-1}(t\otimes x)=t\otimes(1\otimes x)$, $\lambda_T(t\otimes s)=t\alpha_T(s)$, and $\lambda_T^{-1}(t)=t\otimes1$. For every transition or coprojection $h:T\to T'$ on this tail, $\theta_{T'}(h\otimes1_{D_i})=(h\otimes1_B)\theta_T$ and $\lambda_{T'}(h\otimes1_{S_i})=h\lambda_T$. Writing $\varphi_i:S_i\to D_i$ for $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, these identifications give $\theta_T(1_T\otimes\varphi_i)\lambda_T^{-1}(t)=t\otimes1$ and $\theta_T(1\otimes x_i)=(\alpha_T\otimes1_B)(x_i)$ for all $t\in T$ and $x_i\in D_i$. No injectivity, flatness or finite-presentation assumptions are imposed.

proof.text: Given compatible ring maps $b_j:S_j\to U$ on $J_i$, for each $k\in I$ choose $j\ge i,k$ and set $c_k=b_j a_{kj}$. If $j,j'$ are two choices, choose $l\ge j,j'$; compatibility gives $b_j a_{kj}=b_l a_{kl}=b_{j'}a_{kj'}$. Thus $c_k$ is independent of the choice, and is a ring map. For $k\le k'$, choose $j\ge i,k'$ to get $c_{k'}a_{kk'}=b_j a_{k'j}a_{kk'}=c_k$. For $k\in J_i$, taking $j=k$ gives $c_k=b_k$.

source.place: Tag 0CBF (lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth), explicit upper-tail cocone extension underlying its filtered-colimit argument.

proof.text: Write $r_k:R\to S_k$ and $r_S:R\to S$ for the structure maps. Give $U$ the $R$-algebra structure $\rho=b_i r_i$. For $j\ge i,k$, $c_k r_k=b_j r_j=b_j a_{ij}r_i=\rho$, so every $c_k$ is an $R$-algebra map. The given colimit universal property supplies a unique $R$-algebra map $b:S\to U$ with $ba_k=c_k$, hence $ba_j=b_j$ on the tail. Any ring map $d:S\to U$ with those tail restrictions satisfies $dr_S=da_i r_i=\rho$ and, choosing $j\ge i,k$, $da_k=da_j a_{kj}=c_k$. It is consequently an $R$-algebra map and equals $b$ by the same uniqueness. This proves the ring-colimit assertion. If $U$ was already an $R$-algebra and the $b_j$ were $R$-algebra maps, $\rho$ is its given structure map, proving the algebra-colimit assertion too.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), applied to the cocone explicitly extended in step 1.

proof.text: For $T=S_j$ or $S$, the transition/cocone equations make $R\to S_i\xrightarrow{\alpha_T}T$ its given $R$-algebra structure. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with its intermediate ring $S=S_i$ and its algebra $A=T$. It supplies a $T$-algebra isomorphism $\theta_T$ with exactly the two asserted pure-tensor formulas. Its hypotheses are commutativity and the scalar tower just verified; no flatness or injectivity is required.

source.place: Tags 00CV (section-tensor-product) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule); algebra cancellation in the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] over $S_i$ to $\mathrm{id}_T$ and $\alpha_T$ to obtain $\lambda_T(t\otimes s)=t\alpha_T(s)$. Its proposed inverse $t\mapsto t\otimes1$ is the canonical algebra inclusion. One composite sends $t$ to $t$; the other sends $t\otimes s$ to $t\alpha_T(s)\otimes1=t\otimes s$ by $S_i$-balancing. Pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so these composites are identities. Both maps preserve the $T$-structure, hence this is the asserted $T$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product), tensor universal property and balancing; algebra universal property as in Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: For a transition or coprojection $h:T\to T'$, $h\alpha_T=\alpha_{T'}$. On $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$ the two sides of the $\theta$-naturality equation are respectively $h(t)\alpha_{T'}(s)\otimes x$ and $h(t\alpha_T(s))\otimes x$, which agree. On $t\otimes s$ the two sides of the $\lambda$ equation are $h(t)\alpha_{T'}(s)$ and $h(t\alpha_T(s))$. All maps are additive, and nested pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], proving both equations on the whole tensor products.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), generation by pure tensors; naturality checked with the explicit formulas.

proof.text: The composite $\theta_T(1_T\otimes\varphi_i)\lambda_T^{-1}$ sends $t$ successively to $t\otimes1$, $t\otimes(1\otimes1)$, and $t\otimes1$, as asserted. For $x_i=s\otimes x$, the second required identity is $\theta_T(1\otimes(s\otimes x))=\alpha_T(s)\otimes x=(\alpha_T\otimes1_B)(s\otimes x)$. Additivity and generation of $D_i$ by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extend it to every $x_i$.
